entities.name: A Just Russia
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
A Just Russia — Patriots — For Truth (Spravedlivaya Rossiya — Patrioty — Za Pravdu), formed as A Just Russia in 2006 by Kremlin orchestration merging three smaller parties (Rodina, Russian Party of Life, and Russian Pensioners' Party) under Sergei Mironov, is Russia's nominally social-democratic opposition party that functions as a 'systemic opposition' — permitted to exist and criticize the government within limits set by the Kremlin, while never challenging Vladimir Putin's power in any fundamental way. Russia's system of 'managed democracy' requires visible multi-party competition without real competitive challenge.

A Just Russia was created by the Kremlin's political technologists as a second 'loyal opposition' party to the Communist Party — giving Russian voters who disliked United Russia (Putin's party) but didn't want communism a third option. Mironov has supported Putin consistently on major foreign policy and national security questions (including the 2022 invasion of Ukraine) while criticizing specific domestic social policies. The party's 2021 merger with Patrioti Rossii and Za Pravdu (a nationalist grouping) broadened its nationalist credentials.

The party holds approximately 27 seats in the State Duma (2021 elections), making it the fourth-largest party. Its social democratic platform — higher wages, stronger social safety net, workers' rights — appeals to nostalgia for Soviet-era social guarantees. The party is considered one of Russia's 'parliamentary parties' (Duma parties) that participate in the Kremlin's managed democratic system without threatening it.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: A Just Russia is the clearest institutional example of Russia's 'managed democracy' — a political party created by the Kremlin specifically to simulate social-democratic opposition while ensuring no real challenge to United Russia's dominance, making it the definitional case study of political theater in an authoritarian system.
